headword: {成功報酬|せいこうほうしゅう}
gloss: contingency fee; success fee; performance-based reward

definitions.gloss: contingency fee; success fee; reward paid only on success
definitions.explanation: A payment that is owed only when a particular result is achieved, such as winning a lawsuit, closing a deal, or recovering money. Common in legal, consulting, and recruiting work, often alongside an upfront retainer.

examples.japanese: {弁護士|べんごし}に{成功報酬|せいこうほうしゅう}を{払|はら}う。
examples.english: I pay the lawyer a contingency fee.

examples.japanese: この{契約|けいやく}は{着手金|ちゃくしゅきん}なしの{成功報酬|せいこうほうしゅう}{制|せい}だ。
examples.english: This contract is contingency-fee-based, with no upfront payment.

examples.japanese: {回収|かいしゅう}できた{金額|きんがく}の{二割|にわり}を{成功報酬|せいこうほうしゅう}として{受|う}け{取|と}る。
examples.english: They receive twenty percent of the amount recovered as a contingency fee.

notes:
Compound of {成功|せいこう} (success) + {報酬|ほうしゅう} (reward, remuneration). The fee is conditional on a result being achieved.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {成功報酬|せいこうほうしゅう}{型|がた}: contingency-fee type (arrangement)
- {成功報酬|せいこうほうしゅう}を{支払|しはら}う: to pay a success fee
- {完全|かんぜん}{成功報酬|せいこうほうしゅう}: pure contingency fee (with no retainer)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {着手金|ちゃくしゅきん}: retainer fee — paid upfront when work begins, regardless of outcome
- {報酬|ほうしゅう}: reward, remuneration — the general term, not tied to success
